verdicts.quote: “Attio implements the standard OAuth 2.0 specification, using the Authorization Code Grant Flow.”
verdicts.reason: Docs offer both API keys and OAuth, and explicitly prefer OAuth 2.0 for multi‑workspace apps—what a multi‑tenant agent would use. ([docs.attio.com](https://docs.attio.com/rest-api/guides/authentication.md))

verdicts.quote: “Submit your app for review to make it available to all users through the Attio App Store.”
verdicts.reason: API tokens are self‑serve and “available on all plans,” but public/cross‑workspace OAuth distribution requires Attio review; unpublished apps are capped at 25 workspaces—this fits “app_review,” not pure “self_serve_free.” ([docs.attio.com](https://docs.attio.com/share/the-publication-lifecycle.md))

verdicts.quote: “Webhooks allow you to listen for changes to data in Attio, for example when a record is updated.”
verdicts.reason: The official OpenAPI covers many domains (Objects/Records, Lists/Entries, Views, Notes, Meetings, Emails, Tasks, Comments/Threads, Call recordings/Transcripts, Files, Workspace members, Webhooks, SQL), indicating a broad surface. ([api.attio.com](https://api.attio.com/openapi/api))

verdicts.quote: “Attio MCP is Attio’s hosted MCP server that gives AI tools secure access to your Attio workspace.”
verdicts.reason: Vendor‑maintained docs confirm an official hosted MCP server; the Attio App listing also labels it an “Official app” and uses OAuth at mcp.attio.com. ([docs.attio.com](https://docs.attio.com/mcp/overview.md))

verdicts.quote: “Publishing requires a review from the Attio team, which can take up to 1 week.”
verdicts.reason: Buildable now with self‑serve API keys and OAuth dev installs, but caveats apply: app review for public OAuth distribution and some endpoints (e.g., SQL) are Enterprise‑gated—so “ready_with_caveats.” ([docs.attio.com](https://docs.attio.com/share/the-publication-lifecycle.md))
